simple: This page explains `AlignOrientation`, a constraint that turns a part to face a certain way. It can match one attachment's rotation to another attachment, or to a goal rotation you set. It only rotates the part, it does not move it. It is great for keeping a hoverboard level or making a turret face a direction.
analogy: It is like a compass needle: wherever you carry it, it keeps turning to point the same way, but it does not move itself anywhere.
keyPoints: `AlignOrientation` applies torque (twisting force) to rotate `Attachment0` to a goal rotation. It never changes position.
To move a part to a spot instead, use `AlignPosition`.
By default only `Attachment0` gets twisted. `ReactionTorqueEnabled` twists both, in equal and opposite directions.
`AlignType` picks which axes matter. `AllAxes` (default) lines up all three; the `PrimaryAxis...` options only react when the main axis is off.
`RigidityEnabled = true` makes it turn as fast as physics allows.
With rigidity off, `MaxTorque`, `MaxAngularVelocity`, and `Responsiveness` set how strong and fast it turns.
`Mode = OneAttachment` ignores `Attachment1` and turns `Attachment0` to match the `CFrame` property, or the `PrimaryAxis` and `SecondaryAxis` you set.

terms.constraint: An object that controls how parts move, like an invisible motor, rope, or hand pushing them. Mover constraints push or spin parts for you.
terms.assembly: A group of parts that are welded or joined together so physics moves them as one piece. A car body plus its welded seats is one assembly.
terms.attachment: A small invisible point you put inside a part. Constraints hook onto attachments, the same way a rope ties onto a hook.
terms.Attachment0 / Attachment1: The two attachment slots a constraint uses. Attachment0 is usually the one that gets pushed; Attachment1 is the other end or the reference point.
terms.orientation: Which way something is turned or facing, like rotated 90 degrees to the left.
terms.torque: A twisting push that makes something rotate.
terms.axis: A direction line used for rotation. Every attachment has a primary axis (its main pointing direction) and a secondary axis.
terms.primary axis: The attachment's main direction, like the direction an arrow points.
terms.CFrame: A value that stores both a position and a rotation. In `OneAttachment` mode, only its rotation part is used as the goal.
terms.responsiveness: How quickly the constraint reacts. Higher means it turns toward the goal faster.
terms.MaxAngularVelocity: The fastest the constraint is allowed to spin the part while lining it up.

example.title: Keep a part facing the same way
example.place: Script inside a Part in Workspace (part not Anchored)
example.code:
local part = script.Parent

local attachment = Instance.new("Attachment")
attachment.Parent = part

local align = Instance.new("AlignOrientation")
align.Attachment0 = attachment
align.Mode = Enum.OrientationAlignmentMode.OneAttachment
-- Goal: turned 45 degrees around the up (Y) axis
align.CFrame = CFrame.Angles(0, math.rad(45), 0)
align.RigidityEnabled = true -- turn to the goal as fast as possible
align.Parent = part
explain: We add an attachment so the constraint can twist the part.
`OneAttachment` mode means the goal comes from the constraint's own `CFrame` property.
`CFrame.Angles(0, math.rad(45), 0)` is a rotation of 45 degrees around the up axis. `math.rad` turns degrees into radians.
`RigidityEnabled = true` makes it snap to that rotation quickly.
Even if something bumps it, the part keeps turning back to face that way.

watchOut: In `TwoAttachment` mode the `CFrame` property is ignored. Switch to `OneAttachment` to use it.
`CFrame.Angles` uses radians. Use `math.rad(45)` for 45 degrees, not just 45.
This only rotates the part. Pair it with `AlignPosition` if you also want it to stay in a spot.
